text:
🪐 StellarHub

 The control center for your Windows PC. 
Live hardware stats, drivers, apps, disk space, cleanup and hardware tests, in one carefully crafted app.

 
 
 
 

 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 The start screen: the planet's ring lights up while it loads 
 Home in 3D: your PC as a model you can rotate (desktops get a tower) 
 
 

 

 📑 Contents

- What it is
- Screenshots
- Modules
- Also included
- Getting started
- Keyboard shortcuts
- Controller support
- Safety
- Privacy
- Code signing policy
- How it's built
- Roadmap
- Contributing
- License and credits

 ✨ What it is

StellarHub brings together the tools that are usually spread across half a dozen programs: a system monitor,
a driver and app updater, an uninstaller that removes leftovers, a disk space analyzer, an optimizer and a
peripheral tester.

Everything works with real data from your PC , everything that changes the system is reversible whenever
possible, and the interface is designed to be a pleasure to use: smooth animations, a configurable starfield and
no cluttered screens.

 🖼️ Screenshots

 
 
 Live Monitor CPU, GPU, memory, disks, network and battery in real time 
 Storage Checker What every folder takes up, on a map you can explore 
 
 
 Program Remover Uninstall and clear the leftovers, with a quarantine to undo 
 Settings Theme, colors, size, sounds, language and almost everything else 
 
 
 Super Optimizer Cleanup, startup, services and performance, always reversible 
 Privacy & Security What can see you, what is open and how well Windows protects you 
 
 
 Program Updater Apps, Windows, Store and components in one queue 
 Driver Updater Drivers from Windows Update, signed by Microsoft 
 
 
 App Hangar Pick apps from a catalog and install them all at once 
 Benchmark Testing Score every component and stress-test your PC 
 
 
 Device Tester Keyboard, screen, speakers, microphone, camera, mouse and controller 
 Scheduled Tasks Maintenance that runs on its own, on your rules 
 
 

 Screenshots were taken with sample data.

 🧩 Modules

 ⌂ Home
Your PC at a glance: the real model, its components as a tile grid or a 3D model you can rotate, live
stats (CPU, GPU, temperatures, memory, disk, network, battery), system health and what needs attention. Each
component opens a detail card with live data; the displays card even shows what is on each monitor right now.

 ∿ Live Monitor
CPU per thread (performance and efficient cores apart), real clock speed, NVIDIA GPU (load, temperature, power,
VRAM), memory, disks with SMART health, network and Wi-Fi, battery wear, processes with their icons, and system
health (failing devices and critical events explained in plain language).

 ⇅ Driver Updater
Drivers come from Windows Update : signed by Microsoft, the same source as Windows Settings. StellarHub has no driver
database of its own. A full driver inventory, search and install with a restore point first, devices with problems or no
longer connected, driver backups , stored versions to roll back to, and history.

 ⌫ Program Remover
Standard, silent or forced uninstall; a leftover scanner with a confidence score and the reason for each item;
a quarantine so everything can be undone; batch uninstall; watched installs (removes exactly what an
installer created); and a hunter mode (point at a window to find out which program it belongs to).

 ↻ Program Updater
App updates through winget , Windows Update, Microsoft Store, system components (.NET, Visual C++, WebView2…)
and developer tools (pip, npm), with release notes and a queue that shows real progress.

 ⇪ App Hangar
Pick apps from a curated catalog of 150+ trusted programs (or search all of winget) and install them in one go,
with real progress. Ready-made kits (Essentials, Gamer, Developer, Creator…), your own kits, and a short code to
set up another PC the same way.

 ▦ Storage Checker
An interactive map of what each folder takes up, WinDirStat style, with zoom and free space in view. As administrator it reads the NTFS master file table directly, so a full drive scan takes seconds. File types,
largest files, duplicates , and comparisons with earlier scans to see what grew.

 ↯ Super Optimizer
Cleanup of temp files and caches, startup apps, services, Windows repairs (SFC, DISM, chkdsk,
network, Windows Update…) with live output, and performance settings (power plan, visual effects, game mode,
hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling), and Debloat : remove preinstalled apps and turn off ads, suggestions,
Widgets, Copilot and Bing in Start search. Everything backed up first and undoable.
A registry cleaner exists too, but it is off by default (Microsoft doesn't usually recommend them, and Windows doesn't
need one to stay fast): turn it on in Settings General Registry cleaner. It is never part of "Optimize everything".
Its backups stay listed in Settings Backups and restore either way.

 ⛨ Privacy & Security
A privacy and security score with plain-language findings: which apps used your camera, microphone or location and
when, antivirus, firewall, Secure Boot, TPM, encryption and patch age, open ports and who can reach them, 20 Windows
tracking settings with undo, and an audit of everything that starts on its own (tasks, services, browser extensions).

 ◷ Benchmark Testing
Test every component or run them all for a StellarHub Score : processor (per core), graphics (WebGL scenes),
memory bandwidth and latency, CrystalDiskMark-style disk tests, an opt-in network test, and a stress test with
live temperatures, clocks and throttling detection. Every run is kept to compare over time.

 ⌨︎ Device Tester
Keyboard (laptop, 100 %, TKL, 75 %, 65 % and several layouts), dead pixels, speakers, microphone, camera and
mouse, with a CPS test .

 ◎ Scheduled Tasks
Maintenance tasks that run on their own: you choose when (a time, at startup, on unplugging, when space runs low…),
under which conditions and what to do.

install.title: Getting started
install.html:
◇ Install it

Download StellarHub-Setup-x.y.z.exe from the latest release and run it. By default it installs for you only, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\StellarHub: no administrator rights and no Windows prompt (the setup also offers Install for all users, into Program Files, which asks Windows once). It adds a Start menu shortcut and can be removed from Settings > Apps like any other program, and the installer creates no scheduled task. Silent installs use /CURRENTUSER (the default) or /ALLUSERS, plus /DIR=...; an existing all-users install is upgraded in place. Requires Windows 10 (1809) or 11, 64-bit; if your PC lacks the WebView2 Runtime, the setup downloads it from Microsoft (and only runs it if it is signed by Microsoft).

After that, StellarHub keeps itself up to date. A per-user install does it with no prompt at all. An all-users install asks Windows once, the first time, and then makes an on-demand StellarHub\Update task (no schedule) so every later update is silent; uninstalling removes it.

Version Example What happens
Big 2.0.0 A window shows what's new and you choose when to update
New features 1.2.0 Downloads in the background and installs the next time you open StellarHub (Settings > Updates > Install new features automatically)
Small fixes 1.2.3 Never interrupts you: it waits in Settings > Updates

Every big version also gets a name: a figure of Greek or Roman mythology that is also a star, moon or constellation, short and easy to say. 2.x is Atlas; feature and fix versions keep the name of their big version. It shows in a corner of every view (v2.1.0 · ATLAS) and on the start screen, engraved on the planet.

Why an antivirus may flag it

StellarHub is new, not code-signed yet and talks to Windows a lot (drivers, services, startup entries, the registry), which is exactly what heuristic and machine-learning detections watch. A few engines have flagged it as "generic" or "suspicious" with no specific malware name, and Kaspersky's System Watcher has stopped 2.0.0 while it ran (PDM:Trojan.Win32.Generic, a verdict on behaviour, not on the file). What is done about it:

  • the program is built by GitHub Actions from this public repository, with PyInstaller's bootloader compiled from source (not the prebuilt one shared by thousands of programs), as a folder, without packers, with a full version resource and application manifest;
  • it installs per user by default (no administrator rights, nothing in Program Files or scheduled tasks), and reads Windows through WMI inside its own process instead of starting hidden PowerShell windows;
  • since 2.1.1 the live data reads the Wi-Fi signal and the NVIDIA card through Windows' and NVIDIA's own libraries inside the process (it used to start netsh every ten seconds and nvidia-smi), PowerShell is never started with -ExecutionPolicy Bypass or -WindowStyle Hidden, the junk cleaner never opens Windows' core processes (such as lsass.exe) or security software to ask what files they use, and an elevated start only looks at its scheduled tasks when there can be something to fix (once per version), instead of at every start;
  • nothing is added to Windows' startup (the Run key) or the Task Scheduler unless you turn on the matching setting;
  • every release is signed by the author and reported to the antivirus vendors as a false positive.

What it still does, all of it visible in the code: it checks GitHub for a new version a few seconds after it opens and, for a version with new features, downloads the installer in the background (checked against the author's signature before it is ever run) to install it at the next start; the storage map (reading the disk's file table) and the cleaner (asking running programs which files they have open, so it never deletes them) work with a few helper copies of itself (StellarHub.exe --multiprocessing-fork ...), only while a scan or a cleanup runs.

If yours stops it, you can check the file yourself (Verifying a download yourself) or scan it on VirusTotal.

◇ Or take it with you (portable)

Download StellarHub-Portable-x.y.z.zip from the same release and unzip it anywhere, for example a USB drive. Run StellarHub.exe inside the StellarHub folder: no installation. It keeps its settings in a Data folder next to it, adds nothing to Windows' startup or scheduled tasks, and updates itself in place like the installed version. The PC needs the WebView2 Runtime (Windows 11 and up-to-date Windows 10 already have it). What StellarHub backs up before changing a PC stays on that PC, so those changes can be undone there.

The installer is not code-signed yet (see the code signing policy), so Windows SmartScreen may say it is from an "unknown publisher". Each release lists the SHA-256 of the setup file and a signature of the author, so you can check it is the original (see Verifying a download yourself).

◇ Run it from source

Needs Python 3.12 or later.

git clone https://github.com/estebanarosemena/StellarHub.git
cd StellarHub
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
pythonw run.py

For development, python run.py --debug opens the developer tools for the interface.

◇ Build the installer
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File packaging\build.ps1

It creates a clean build environment with pinned versions, runs the tests, builds StellarHub.exe with PyInstaller and packs it with Inno Setup 6.7+ into dist\. The app is built as a folder (not a single self-extracting file) and without UPX, so it starts as fast as running from source and does not look like a packed executable to antivirus software. Release builds also compile PyInstaller's bootloader from source: the prebuilt one is byte-for-byte the same in thousands of programs, some of them malware, and antivirus machine-learning models match on it. The build installs the pinned PyInstaller from its source package with PYINSTALLER_COMPILE_BOOTLOADER=1 and fails if packaging\check_bootloader.py finds the result identical to the official wheel's. Locally it compiles it when Visual Studio's C++ tools are found (STELLARHUB_COMPILE_BOOTLOADER=1 forces it, =0 skips it) and otherwise keeps the prebuilt one and says so. StellarHub.exe carries a complete version resource (packaging\make_assets.py) and an application manifest (packaging\StellarHub.manifest).

Releases are built from this repository by GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/build.yml), with the same script.

◇ Administrator mode

StellarHub works without it, in limited mode. Installing drivers, cleaning system files, repairing Windows or reading the CPU temperature and disk SMART data require it; the app suggests it quietly when needed.

When something you click needs it, StellarHub asks in a small window; Open as administrator reopens it elevated right where you were (same module, tab, search and scroll) and picks up the action you asked for, with its usual confirmation. Always open as administrator (Settings > Administrator) uses a scheduled task only in an install for all users, whose program folder only administrators can change. In a per-user install the folder is yours, so any program you run could replace StellarHub.exe there: Windows asks each time instead, and a task left by an earlier version is removed the next time StellarHub runs as administrator.

Many PCs (especially desktop motherboards) don't report the CPU temperature to Windows at all. In that case StellarHub reads it from LibreHardwareMonitor, HWiNFO (with Shared Memory Support on) or Core Temp if one of them is running, and says which one it used.
